execution_policy.branch_layout: The working directory is an offline export of the pull request's repository. Local branch `main` is the merge-base and local branch `review-head`, which is checked out, is the head under review; the change under review is the committed range `main...review-head`. There is no remote, no network, and nothing outside this attempt's directories is available.
execution_policy.allowance: Reading the clone is always permitted. Commands may be run only as the target's allowance below states, offline, with a five-minute limit per command; scratch files go under the work directory; nothing may be added to or changed in the clone, whose tree identity is checked before and after the review.

deviations.what: After the pilot's four attempts (att-001 to att-004), bench/tools moved from the frozen metric_code_revision 33c78ced23988a540ced1786e0e2a97d20448831 to 02005197f6b4df4d6a1471d548ca9f00d69112e9, which fixes normalize_review.py's Codex parsing (the 'Full review comments:' marker Codex CLI 0.156.1 writes for several findings, and a summary-only review with rollout verdict 'patch is correct' read as empty) and attempt_audit.py's reading of a slash after a glob character as an absolute path. The change touches no reviewer input or execution condition. The claude-builtin attempts att-001 and att-003 re-normalize and re-audit identically. The codex-default attempts att-002 and att-004 were stopped by the old normalizer after reviews that ran to completion; their disposition is decided in a later deviation. Every later attempt is filed with the fixed tools.

The codex-default attempts att-002 and att-004 are re-filed from their own outputs, with no replacement. Their reviews ran to a zero exit; only the wrapper's normalizer stopped them, and the repair in the first deviation changed no reviewer input or execution condition, so method §3's rerun rule does not apply. bench/tools moved to 6f61765dbfd07d70539ffea90779f671be0af5f4, whose file_attempt.py --replay supersedes a stop written only for a failed normalization after a zero exit once the replayed normalizer parses, keeping it as stop.recorded.json. Re-filed at that revision, att-002 is valid completed with 3 parsed items and a clean audit, and att-004 is valid completed and empty; each keeps its stop instant as completed_at and a null payload_validated_at. Their usage is unchanged; their transcript archives were rewritten with new hashes and passed the restoration check. The claude-builtin records att-001 and att-003 are not re-filed.

bench/tools moved to 552a6f827dae7dc05ec8a951941f49437faf11fe, which corrects the glob fix of the first deviation: at 02005197f6b4df4d6a1471d548ca9f00d69112e9 attempt_audit.py no longer read a word that starts with a slash and then a glob character (/*/x, /*/*/.config/bench) as an absolute path, so such a read outside the allowed roots went unflagged. Glob characters now stay part of an absolute path and the whole path is judged against the roots; a first segment that starts with a glob counts once another slash follows, and a slash after a glob in a relative word still continues that word. The change touches no reviewer input or execution condition. The paths extracted from the commands recorded in the audit.json of att-001 to att-004 are identical at 6f61765dbfd07d70539ffea90779f671be0af5f4 and at the new revision, so no filed attempt's audit or disposition changes and none is re-filed. Every later attempt is filed with the corrected tools.

bench/tools moved to f1a4343038f5d182231f83e9bb8328060dd8cdce, which restores a flag the first deviation's glob fix dropped: bash 5.1 expands a path segment such as .*, .? or .[.] to .., so cat .*/.*/<path> reads above the attempt directory, and at 02005197f6b4df4d6a1471d548ca9f00d69112e9 attempt_audit.py no longer flagged it, where the frozen revision had, by misreading the slash after the glob as an absolute path. A segment that starts with a literal dot and can match .. is now judged as .., in absolute paths, relative operands, runs inside quoted scripts and cd targets, and path-like runs inside a word now include glob characters. The change touches no reviewer input or execution condition. Over the commands recorded in the audit.json of att-001 to att-004, the paths extracted at 552a6f827dae7dc05ec8a951941f49437faf11fe and at the new revision differ only in att-002, whose two commands through ../clone-cache/venv/lib/python*/site-packages no longer also yield the truncated run ending at python; every path extracted is inside the attempt directory at both revisions, so no filed attempt's audit or disposition changes and none is re-filed. Every later attempt is filed with the corrected tools.

bench/tools moved to a49dd79d82b58267de4fa9a83e60f3e6a4aa68e2, which extends the fourth deviation's fix to ~ paths: attempt_audit.py's ~ pattern stopped at a glob character, so cat ~/.*/.*/<path>, which bash 5.1 expands to a read two levels above the attempt's home, went unflagged at 02005197f6b4df4d6a1471d548ca9f00d69112e9 and at f1a4343038f5d182231f83e9bb8328060dd8cdce, where the frozen revision had flagged it by misreading the slash after the glob as an absolute path. A ~ path now keeps its glob characters, a dot-led segment that can match .. is judged as .., and the path is normalised once expanded against the fresh home. The change touches no reviewer input or execution condition. None of the commands recorded in the audit.json of att-001 to att-004 contains ~, and the paths extracted from them are identical at f1a4343038f5d182231f83e9bb8328060dd8cdce and at the new revision, so no filed attempt's audit or disposition changes and none is re-filed. Every later attempt is filed with the corrected tools.

Scope of the read audit, decided by the maintainer after the pilot: method §3 item 5's control guards against a reviewer's accidental reads outside the allowed roots, which name their path, and not against reads a reviewer disguises on purpose. Spellings the shell rewrites before running (a variable, a quoted or escaped dot glob, brace expansion, ~user, a symlink planted in the clone or the fresh home and read through) are recorded as known blind spots in the run README's pilot section, not repaired during this run. No tool, reviewer input or execution condition changes, and no filed attempt changes.

bench/tools moved to 33b0c25e694cc2f276ed39347198a6178c5a0752, which fixes attempt_audit.py's network rule. The old pattern matched a network tool's name anywhere it followed a non-word character, so a Go file name before a space (`internal/notify.go internal/...`, `--path internal/backup.go --chunk 1`), prose inside a Python heredoc, and the offline go commands the (m) and (q) allowances grant (`GOPROXY=off GOTOOLCHAIN=local ... go test`) all read as network commands. The rule now counts a tool only in command position, judges `go` offline when the command sets GOPROXY=off and GOTOOLCHAIN=local before it, counts npm, pnpm, yarn and pip only with a subcommand that reaches a registry (target (o)'s allowance permits a pnpm rebuild), and skips a heredoc body unless a shell reads it. The first two grid attempts ran on (q): att-005 (A) was filed harness-invalid on five such false network flags alone and is re-audited with file_attempt.py --replay to valid completed, with no replacement; att-006 (B) is re-audited the same way and stays harness-invalid on its own read and write of /tmp/pr.diff, outside the attempt's roots although the policy sends scratch files to the work directory and its TMPDIR was there, and is replaced under method §3 item 4. The change touches no reviewer input or execution condition; the pilot's att-001 to att-004 have no command the old or new rule flags.

bench/tools moved to f563ef22a3df3ea3d367c619dbb3bafe45561f4f: attempt_audit.py no longer starts an absolute path at a slash that follows ':/', so a URL's authority inside a command (`new Request('http://localhost/')` in att-012's scratch script) is not read as the path /localhost; `file:///<path>` still yields the path. att-012 ((p) / D / 1) was filed harness-invalid on that one flag alone and is re-audited with file_attempt.py --replay to valid completed, with no replacement. att-011 ((p) / C / 1) finished while the fix was being tested and is re-audited the same way; its audit is unchanged and it stays valid completed. No filed attempt other than att-012 has a command containing ':/'. The change touches no reviewer input or execution condition.

bench/tools moved to eb8cad3720f4adb4e175145769b85f61eaa8846c: a path outside the allowed roots is now a read-audit violation only when it names something on disk when the audit runs (a glob by any match), the rule method §3 item 4 already applies to ancestor guidance files; the absent ones are listed in audit.json as absent_outside_paths. The text audit extracts slash-led words from scratch code, and on the TypeScript targets it read route strings ('/a', '/i'), JSX closing tags (</Form>, </button>, </Field.Root>), import specifiers (/react, /utils) and a sed pattern (s#/clone/src/hono#...) as absolute paths; none exists, so nothing was read. att-013 ((p) / A / 1) and att-014 ((r) / C / 1) were filed harness-invalid on such paths alone and are re-audited with file_attempt.py --replay to valid completed, with no replacement. Running the new audit over every other filed attempt changes nothing: att-006 stays flagged because /tmp/pr.diff, which it wrote, exists (it is already replaced by att-007). Under the scope the sixth deviation records, a read of a path that does not exist reveals nothing; a file an attempt deletes before the audit runs is a further blind spot of the same kind. The change touches no reviewer input or execution condition.

bench/tools moved to 2da77b4668fae5150eb37142959b8b5c3ad138c7: attempt_audit.py resolved every path through its symlinks, so target (i)'s provisioned venv interpreter, <cache>/venv/bin/python, a link uv makes to its CPython under ~/.local/share/uv, read as a path outside the roots; the pnpm targets' corepack bin links would have done the same. A path inside the roots as written may now leave them through symlinks whose ctime is before the dispatch instant in the attempt's timing.json (plus one second, the stamp being truncated), which are the harness's; a symlink the reviewer makes is later and still violates, so a link planted in the clone or the work directory during the attempt is now caught, narrowing the sixth deviation's blind spot (the lexical ~/<link>/../ case stays one). att-018 ((i) / A / 1) was filed harness-invalid on its six uses of the venv interpreter alone and is re-audited with file_attempt.py --replay to valid completed, with no replacement; its venv link was made at 05:18:09.34Z against a dispatch stamp of 05:18:09Z. Running the new audit over every other filed attempt (att-001 to att-020) leaves each audit unchanged. The change touches no reviewer input or execution condition.

bench/tools moved to fd5d2e9aa009f6dad1d5fbd3ba661408a0089f2c: attempt_audit.py resolved every Claude Bash call from the clone root, but Claude Code keeps a cd between calls and records the directory each call ran in as the transcript line's cwd. att-031 ((o) / A / 1) had cd'd into packages/integrations/vercel in an earlier call and then ran `C=$(cd ../../.. && pwd)`, which is the clone root; resolved from the clone it read as /home/jack/.t3/bench-runs, and the attempt was filed harness-invalid on that alone. The audit now treats a Claude call's recorded cwd as its working directory, as it treats a Codex call's workdir; att-031 is re-audited with file_attempt.py --replay to valid completed, with no replacement. The same resolution also catches a climb it used to miss (cat ../../<outside> from a subdirectory). Running the new audit over every other filed attempt (att-001 to att-034) changes no violation list; att-016's recorded working directories change. The change touches no reviewer input or execution condition.

bench/tools moved to 216e50710b7df769e0e2b0323d4dfa15da8c6574: attempt_audit.py counted a cd target as a read, and tokenized heredoc bodies as command operands in its relative-path walk. att-059 ((l) / B / 2) ran `cd <attempt>/clone-work 2>/dev/null || cd /tmp; cat > t.js <<'E' ...`; the work directory existed, so the fallback never ran, and t.js was written there (no /tmp/t.js exists), but /tmp was flagged and the attempt filed harness-invalid on that alone. A cd target is no longer itself a read; what is read relative to it still is (cd <outside> && cat <file> is flagged when the file exists), and a heredoc body is skipped by the relative walk unless a shell reads it, as the network rule already did; absolute paths inside a body are still judged. att-059 is re-audited with file_attempt.py --replay to valid completed, with no replacement. Running the new audit over every other filed attempt (att-001 to att-060) changes no violation list. A bare listing after a cd outside the roots (cd <dir> && ls) is a blind spot of the kind the sixth deviation records. The change touches no reviewer input or execution condition.

bench/tools moved to 645607ee460db2e2f03ab38069cdfd3f5300e992: attempt_audit.py's network rule read inside quoted text, so the alternation in att-079's search pattern, rg -n -A12 "func \(ac \*addrConn\) resetTransport|...|go ac.resetTransport", read as a pipe into a go command. Quoted text is now masked before the rule runs, except a script opened right after -c and a $(...) inside double quotes, which the shell runs. att-079 ((m) / A / 2) was filed harness-invalid on that one flag alone and is re-audited with file_attempt.py --replay to valid completed, with no replacement. Running the new audit over every other filed attempt (att-001 to att-080) changes no violation list. The change touches no reviewer input or execution condition.

bench/tools moved to 503aba4933483b0c3db9f23ad60a696cbba029fa, closing two gaps the thirteenth deviation's network rule left, both found in review of the grid: a script handed to a shell through a combined option (zsh -fc "curl ...", bash -lc '...') was masked as quoted data, and a go command was judged offline whenever GOPROXY=off and GOTOOLCHAIN=local appeared anywhere earlier in the command, so in `GOPROXY=off GOTOOLCHAIN=local go test ./...; go mod download` the second go passed. The rule now recognizes any shell's -c option, combined or not, and judges each go invocation by its own prefix assignments over the variables exported earlier and not unset or overridden since; a bare NAME=value statement, which go does not inherit, no longer counts. Re-running the audit over all 83 filed attempts changes no violation list, so no attempt is re-filed. The change touches no reviewer input or execution condition.
